title: SLC7A2 regulates the inflammation and apoptosis of LPS-induced human lung epithelial cells through TLR4/NF-κB pathway.
Genome architecture and duplication-associated functional diversification in the carnivorous plant Sarracenia purpurea
summary: The repeated evolution of complex traits raises the question of how genomes generate ecological novelty while preserving developmental organization. We present a chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for the carnivorous purple pitcher plant, Sarracenia purpurea, and investigate how two contrasting modes of gene duplication have shaped its genome and functional repertoire: ancient polyploidy, which leaves duplicated genes in conserved chromosomal regions (syntenic duplicates), and local tandem duplication, which generates neighboring gene copies. We compare these duplication classes across nine angiosperms. The genome shows a mosaic of conserved and fractionated duplicated regions reflecting differential retention and loss of genes following ancient polyploidy and later restructuring. Comparison with noncarnivorous Actinidia (kiwifruit) identifies 18 syntenic and nine tandem Gene Ontology (GO) Biological Process term-duplication-class combinations enriched in Sarracenia but not significantly enriched in Actinidia. Syntenic enrichments include meristem maintenance, organ-boundary specification, cuticle development, and hormonal regulation; tandem enrichments include defense responses, oxidative stress, jasmonic-acid biosynthesis, leaf senescence, and oligopeptide transport. Across the carnivorous genera Sarracenia, Nepenthes, Utricularia, and Pinguicula, we identify 19 syntenic and two tandem-associated biological processes showing significant enrichment in all four lineages, revealing striking functional commonalities across multiple evolutionary origins of carnivory despite their divergent trap morphologies and ecological strategies. Among Sarracenia genes differentially expressed in at least one comparison of flower, pitcher-leaf, and root tissues, tandem-class genes exhibit larger maximum absolute expression differences and greater GO richness and effective breadth at matched numbers of annotated homologs. These results highlight the complementary evolutionary contributions of ancient genome duplication and local gene-family expansion to the developmental and ecological diversification of carnivorous plants.

title: Differential DNA methylation and transcriptome revealed enhanced photosynthetic recovery and ROS modulation to promote cold tolerance in Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica.
summary: Indica rice, being a tropical crop, is highly sensitive to cold temperatures. Cold stress affects vegetative growth, photosynthetic efficiency and reproductive features. Screening diverse landraces to identify novel alleles associated with cold tolerance can be an approach to develop cold resilient indica rice. We have characterized a boro germplasm, CB1, with an efficient germination rate and growth vigor when treated with chilling temperatures. CB1 seedlings show a higher survival rate compared to IR36 when subjected to prolonged chilling stress. Biochemical analysis indicated efficient ROS modulation, higher chlorophyll content, enhanced photosystem II efficiency and unique stomatal traits, leading to higher relative water content in CB1 plants during stress and recovery. Germplasm-specific DNA methylome and transcriptome uniquely regulate the expression of chlorophyll biosynthesis, photosystem, & light harvesting complex and ROS scavenger genes in CB1 seedlings during stress recovery. Interestingly, high D1 protein turnover in CB1 promotes damage repair of PSII for efficient photosynthesis. Furthermore, key transcription factors for stomatal development and expression of photosynthetic genes were upregulated in CB1 during stress recovery. Notably, higher expression of GLK1 and enrichment of GLK1 targets were observed in CB1 plants during chilling stress and recovery. Taken together, our results indicate that GLK1 and WRKY40 negatively regulates the inhibitory role of ABI5 for efficient photosynthetic recovery to enhance cold tolerance in CB1 rice.

title: Two copy-number forms of the Kala4/OsB2 upstream duplication in purple rice revealed by a telomere-to-telomere genome of landrace ZN65
summary: Background: Black and purple pericarp in rice requires activation of the regulator Kala4/OsB2. The canonical black-rice allele is a promoter rearrangement that was described from DNA gel blots and amplified fragments, and its sequence is unavailable. Whether pigmented landraces carry one upstream structure or several is therefore unknown. We examined this region in the purple-pericarp landrace Mojiang ZN65 and its distribution in sequenced rice germplasm. Results: We assembled a gap-free telomere-to-telomere genome of ZN65 (395.1 Mb; all 24 telomeres). Upstream of Kala4/OsB2, a 5.87-kb segment (block A) and a 6.0-kb segment that contains the first two annotated exons of OsB2 were each present in three non-tandem copies. The arrangement was reproduced by an independent HiFi-only assembly and was spanned by three Nanopore reads. Among 2,913 accessions of the 3,000 Rice Genomes panel, read depth detected block A gain in 29 (1.0%), 17 at three or more copies and 12 at two. All 29 carried read pairs joining block A to the OsB2 5' segment, and none of 58 matched controls did. A junction specific to the third copy was found in 16 of these 17 and in 2 of these 12. Among 2,055 accessions with recorded seed-coat colour, 18 of 19 purple accessions carried the gain, and purple was recorded for 9 of 13 and 9 of 11 carriers of the two classes. Among 210 NCBI assemblies and 264 Genome Warehouse materials, five carried the junctions with two copies of block A, and one, the Chinese accession Momi, carried three copies, which its Nanopore reads confirmed. An elevated OsKala3 promoter-repeat depth ratio was found in 21 of 29 carriers, and four purple carriers lacked it. Conclusions: ZN65 provides a gap-free, read-supported sequence of a Kala4/OsB2 upstream duplication that occurs in at least two copy-number forms in purple rice. Its gene-proximal part has the same kinds of elements in the same order as the published description of the canonical black-rice allele, although the segment lengths differ. Both forms were found in purple accessions, and the additional copy showed no relation to recorded colour. Its effect on OsB2 expression remains untested.

title: A sunflower FLS2 guides reconstruction of immune-evasive Xanthomonas flg22 recognition across divergent FLS2 backgrounds
summary: Immune-evasive Xanthomonas flg22 epitopes pose a challenge to FLS2-mediated immune surveillance. A further challenge is to reconstruct their recognition across divergent FLS2 backgrounds with a limited number of amino-acid substitutions. AlphaFold 3 (AF3) screening of 256 natural FLS2 homologues identified sunflower HaFLS2-1, responsive to flg22Xcc and flg22Xoo in transient ROS assays. We validated flg22Xcc recognition by in planta ligand-association assays and immune responses in stable Arabidopsis lines. Guided by HaFLS2-1 ligand-proximal residues, iterative AF3 searches generated PsFLS2 (Salicaceae) and TjFLS2 (Apocynaceae) variants recognising flg22Xcc with ten or fewer substitutions. Single-residue reversions revealed functional contributions from over half of recurrent substitutions in both backgrounds. RcFLS2 (Rosaceae) variants acquired flg22Xcc responsiveness. In tomato SlFLS2 (Solanaceae), three substitutions significantly enhanced flg22Xcc responses, while all three variants carrying two to four substitutions acquired flg22Xoo responsiveness. These findings demonstrate the utility of AF3-guided natural-receptor discovery and iterative engineering for reconstructing and expanding flg22 recognition.

title: Acetate promotes nutritional adaptation in Escherichia coli
summary: Escherichia coli often releases acetate in its environment where it can accumulate to concentrations high enough to inhibit the bacterium's own growth. Here, we demonstrate that acetate promotes E. coli adaptation to nutrient changes by accelerating growth resumption, with as little as 250 M acetate being sufficient to shorten the lag phase by several hours. Acetate was found to be consumed via acetyl-CoA synthetase very early after the nutrient change. Transcriptomics, metabolomics and 13C-isotope labeling experiments show that acetate replenishes metabolic pools in the tricarboxylic acid cycle and upper glycolysis. Single-cell analyses reveal that acetate increases the adaptation speed of individual cells switching to the new nutrient. We conclude that the reuse of excreted acetate by E. coli facilitates nutritional adaptation by transiently replenishing central metabolite pools. This work identifies an unexpected role of acetate in the nutritional adaptation of E. coli, providing new insights into the physiological relevance of overflow metabolism.

title: Laterality of subcortical structures predicts spontaneous brain dynamics
summary: Subcortical structures contribute to neocortical activity through extensive circuits supporting cognition and behaviour. Although these anatomical connections are well established, how subcortical structure relates to neocortical oscillations remains poorly understood. Previous studies have linked subcortical volume asymmetries to cortical alpha modulation during attention tasks, but whether these relationships extend to spontaneous brain activity remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether hemispheric asymmetries in subcortical volume are associated with lateralised resting-state oscillatory power. We analysed structural MRI and resting-state magnetoencephalography (MEG) data from 532 healthy adults in the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (CamCAN) cohort, correlating volume asymmetries of seven subcortical structures with MEG power asymmetries across four frequency bands. We found that globus pallidus asymmetry was positively associated with alpha-band power lateralisation, extending previous task-based findings to the resting state. Within the striatum, putamen asymmetry was positively associated with frontal beta-band lateralisation, whereas caudate asymmetry was negatively associated with posterior beta- and delta-band lateralisation. Hippocampal asymmetry was negatively associated with frontal delta-band lateralisation. Despite the complexity of cortico-subcortical connectivity, these findings reveal distinct frequency-specific relationships between subcortical anatomy and spontaneous neocortical activity that align with the established functional roles of these structures. Our results demonstrate that these relationships can be detected non-invasively in resting state without requiring direct recording of deep brain regions, providing a foundation for investigating whether resting-state MEG can identify early functional changes associated with subcortical neurodegeneration.

title: Connexin43 drives mitochondrial biogenesis and organelle stress in BRAF-mutant melanoma cells
summary: Metabolic flexibility helps cancer cells survive targeted therapy, and BRAF-mutant melanoma rewires mitochondrial metabolism in response to BRAF/MEK inhibitors (BRAF/MEKi). We previously showed that connexin43 (Cx43) acts as a tumour suppressor in BRAF-mutant melanoma and enhances the response to BRAF/MEKi. Here, we investigated whether mitochondrial remodelling contributes to these effects. Cx43 upregulation promoted mitochondrial biogenesis including selective increase of CI and CV, enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), and increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, alongside DRP1-associated mitochondrial fragmentation. Despite enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis and OXPHOS, Cx43 upregulation was associated with respiratory chain remodelling, characterised by loss of complex IV, increased ER and mitochondrial stress, and enhanced mTORC1-associated signalling. These changes were accompanied by an adaptive unfolded protein response that did not engage the pro-apoptotic ATF4-CHOP axis. Notably, BRAF/MEK inhibition largely attenuated the mitochondrial biogenesis phenotype and most of the stress markers associated with Cx43 upregulation, while promoting mitochondrial network elongation and markedly increasing mitochondrial ROS. Despite this impact, Cx43-expressing tumour cells retained higher membrane potential, ROS levels and survival under glucose-limiting conditions. Collectively, these findings reveal a dissociation between the mitochondrial effects of Cx43 and its enhancement of the response to BRAF/MEKi, highlighting the complexity of Cx43-mediated metabolic regulation in BRAF-mutant melanoma. By distinguishing mitochondrial remodelling from therapeutic sensitisation, this study provides new insights into the response to BRAF/MEK inhibition and highlights mTORC1-associated signalling and mitochondrial oxidative stress as potential therapeutic vulnerabilities for further investigation.
